You are running as the daily research agent for quantloop. CLAUDE.md is loaded; follow its daily procedure exactly.

Today's run, in order:

1. Read state/summary.md, LEDGER.md, FINDINGS.md, hypotheses/backlog.md, the newest file in notes/ and state/bench/README.md if it is there (a line under `Not read` there, for the champion or for a config in a slot, goes at the top of notes/<today>.md, word for word). Run `gh pr list --state closed --limit 5` and, for any PR closed in the last few days by the gate, `gh pr view <n> --comments` to read why.
2. Run `python -m bot.wide` (it only reads; never add `--collect`). If any line of what it prints begins with FAILED, STALE or SETTING NOT USED, those lines go at the top of notes/<today>.md, word for word, whatever else this run does. Write that note for them alone if the run would not otherwise write one: nothing else tells Fin.
3. Read the Fill cap section of state/summary.md. A buy stopped by the cap that no note of the last 8 days in notes/ reports goes in notes/<today>.md, with which of the three CLAUDE.md names it is (a resize, a whipsaw or a loop, read from that account's decisions.csv and trades.csv) or that it was a new strategy's first buy; a loop goes at the top. Write that note for it alone if the run would not otherwise write one.
4. If the ledger's `## Results` section has a verdict that FINDINGS.md does not reflect yet, update FINDINGS.md first (finding plus calibration line). FINDINGS.md stays under 30,000 characters (`wc -m FINDINGS.md`): if an addition would take it over, condense it first as CLAUDE.md says, or the gate fails the pull request.
5. If no note dated since the last Monday (UTC) has a `## Weekly review` section, do the weekly review CLAUDE.md describes and put it in notes/<today>.md under `## Weekly review`, below any lines for Fin at its top.
6. Determine which slots are free (listed at the top of state/summary.md; `python -m bot.slot` confirms it).
7. If no slot is free: do the review described in CLAUDE.md, write notes/<today>.md, update hypotheses/backlog.md if you have a real idea, and commit. Do not change any configs/challenger<k>.yaml or bot/strategy.py unless you found a bug that does not confound a running test.
8. If a slot is free: choose a hypothesis from a different family than the tests already running, write one ledger entry and change that one slot's config (and bot/strategy.py only if new logic is needed, with tests). Read it on the bench first, before the tests and the long backtest: `python -m bot.bench --config configs/challenger<k>.yaml --quick` (run it with the Bash tool's `timeout` set to 1800000, which is 30 minutes in milliseconds: it replays five years; never add `--save`; if it runs out of time, do not run it again). If the bench reads the idea as no sign of timing (it beats fewer than half its twins), it does not go in the slot: undo its config change and ledger entry, put it back in the backlog with its Bench line, and try one other idea at most (two readings a run); if none qualifies, leave the slot in cash and say why in the note. Otherwise run `python -m pytest tests -q` (with the Bash tool's `timeout` set to 1200000, which is 20 minutes: the tests take six or seven) and `python -m bot.backtest --config configs/challenger<k>.yaml --gate`, put the metrics and the skill line in the ledger entry's Backtest line (the gate line must say PASS) and the bench's last line, the one that begins `Bench:`, in its Bench line with what you make of it (or `not taken:` and why in a few words, if no reading could be taken), remove the idea from the backlog, delete any scratch files, and commit with first line `H<n>: <title>`.
9. Before committing, run `git diff --name-only origin/main` and confirm nothing listed in PROTECTED.txt appears and at most one configs/challenger<k>.yaml changed. If a protected file changed, revert it with `git checkout origin/main -- <path>`.
10. Commit with `git add -A && git commit -m "<message>"`. Do not push; the workflow pushes and opens the PR. If you made no changes at all, say so in one line and stop.

Finish with a short plain English summary of what you did and why.
